parallel.requirements: Recognized ESM-only .mjs output, manual --a parsing, exact Schema print output, zero external dependencies, and black-box observation via the executable.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Although swarm mode was entered, the parent decided the task was small and sequential, did not delegate, and owned probing, implementation, verification, and final delivery itself.
parallel.implementation: Created fields.mjs with field classes and Schema, argparser.mjs with required --a handling and help/error formatting, and test2.mjs importing local .mjs modules and printing the schema representation.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Integrated the entry point directly against the local modules in /output and delivered test2.mjs plus two library files; no child handoff or merge step occurred.
parallel.verification: Ran the executable for normal, missing, equals-form, help, unknown, and missing-value cases, then compared Node behavior while normalizing the program-name difference.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: Official evaluation still failed 59 of 163 cases; trajectory evidence points to a shared acceptance mismatch, especially the accepted program-name normalization in argparse-style output, rather than a coordination-specific failure.

serial.requirements: Recognized ESM-only .mjs output, manual --a parsing, exact Schema print output, zero external dependencies, and executable-based observation.
serial.plan_and_ownership: Single main actor owned the whole solution, probing executable behavior, planning four modules, writing all files, running checks, and delivering the final response.
serial.implementation: Created fields.mjs field factories, schema.mjs for Schema string behavior, argparse.mjs for required --a parsing, and test2.mjs wiring those modules together.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Integrated the entry point with schema, fields, and argparse modules in /output and delivered the four-file ESM implementation without delegation or merge boundaries.
serial.verification: Ran executable probes, diffed main success output against Node, and checked Node error/help behavior for missing, missing-value, unknown, and help cases.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: Official evaluation still failed 59 of 163 cases; the trajectory shows it did not compare full error/help text against the executable and accepted test2.mjs as the program name.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the required ESM .mjs files, manual --a parsing, exact output alignment, zero dependencies, and executable observation.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial recognized the same migration requirements and used the executable to inspect output and argparse behavior.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement-recognition difference; both missed or tolerated the same acceptance-sensitive program-name mismatch in CLI diagnostics.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel ran in swarm-enabled mode but chose direct parent ownership for all work and used no child agents.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used a single main actor and no delegation, owning all probing, implementation, testing, and closure itself.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The only decomposition difference is module layout: parallel used three files, while serial separated Schema into a fourth module.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel had no child briefs or handoffs; its only interfaces were local imports between argparser.mjs, fields.mjs, and test2.mjs.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial likewise had no child briefs or handoffs; it defined local interfaces among argparse.mjs, schema.mjs, fields.mjs, and test2.mjs.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No cross-agent context or interface transfer existed. Serial introduced a separate Schema module, while parallel colocated Schema with field classes.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel probed the executable, wrote Schema and field classes in fields.mjs, wrote a parser in argparser.mjs, and wired test2.mjs to print schema.toString().
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial probed the executable, wrote fields.mjs and schema.mjs separately, wrote argparse.mjs, and wired test2.mjs to print schema.toString().
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both implemented the same observable happy-path behavior; serial had a cleaner module split, while parallel modeled KEYWORD as a class reference in test2.mjs.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: There were no child results to retrieve or join; the parent wrote all deliverables and ended after its own verification loop.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: There were no child results; the single actor wrote all files and ended after local verification.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No result-lifecycle coordination difference exists because neither trajectory produced child results or pending child work.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel wrote all files from the main actor in a single workspace and no concurrent actor touched the same or related files.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote all files from the main actor in a single workspace and no concurrent actor touched the workspace.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No shared-state race or merge difference exists; both produced valid artifact directories, with parallel containing three files and serial containing four.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel compared several success and error/help cases but normalized test2.mjs to test2_executable in its check and then claimed all cases matched.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial diffed the main success output and ran Node-side error/help checks, but did not fully compare those diagnostics against the executable.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had broader comparative checking but masked the program-name text difference; serial had less complete error-output comparison. Both nevertheless failed the official evaluator at the same rate.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel completed quickly, did not time out, used no children, and closed after presenting files and verification results.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial also completed without timeout, used no children, and closed after presenting its files and verification results.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No budget-related coordination difference exists; serial took longer wall-clock time, but neither run shows a displaced parallel task or unfinished child work.

outcome_analysis.explanation: Both current official evaluations completed and both runs failed with the same 104 of 163 score. The trajectories differ only in direct implementation structure and verification method: parallel ran with swarm mode enabled but did not spawn children and used a three-file layout, while serial used a four-file layout. Both accepted argparse program-name differences during their own checks, so the paired outcome is not explained by a parallel coordination episode.
parallel_contributors: No executed child-agent mechanism; direct parent implementation despite swarm mode.
Verification normalized the program-name difference and then treated CLI cases as matching.
serial_contributors: No delegation; single actor implemented a four-file ESM solution.
Verification checked main output by diff and Node-side diagnostics but did not fully compare error/help text against the executable.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel bundled Schema with field classes in fields.mjs; serial split Schema into schema.mjs.
Both implementations used the Node script name test2.mjs in argparse-style diagnostics rather than proving byte-for-byte parity for the executable name in all checked cases.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; shared ordinary implementation or acceptance mismatch, not an evidenced concurrency-specific contributor
